4th Period.workingNow: Watching our PII and HTML intro videos and completing the notes document before starting your About Me page.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A complete About Me page (copied from the Example file) with header/body structure, formatted favorites text, at least one resized image with a caption, and a table.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can explain why personal information should stay private online and begin building my About Me page using header and body tags.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.IC.20 — Keep login credentials and personal information private when using networked devices and online tools; CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.13 — Create prototypes using structured code, organized into separate linked pages, to fulfill a design requirement.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.5 — Listening actively to spoken English in a range of social and academic contexts.
agenda: Warm-Up: Self-paced Wayground — classroom expectations review (5 min)
Watch: intro to HTML video (8 min)
Complete guided notes document on both videos (10 min)
You do: copy the Example file, rename to about-me.html, add a header (15 min)
Exit Ticket: paste your header tag (4 min)
4th Period.connections: Last week you got GitHub Pages live with a single pasted image. Today, before writing more code, we cover the ground rules — what to keep private online and what HTML actually is — then start your real About Me page by copying our Example file. By Friday this page will be complete with your favorites, an image, and a table.

6th Period.workingNow: Talking through how a traffic light "knows" when to change states.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A Sprite Lab or Game Lab project where a scene or sprite has at least two states triggered by an event.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can describe how an event triggers a state change so that I understand how games track different modes.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.10 — Use flowcharts and/or pseudocode to design solutions to complex problems.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.1 — Exchanging information and ideas with others through collaborative discussions.
agenda: Warm-Up: Self-paced Wayground — classroom expectations review (5 min)
I do: traffic light state machine example on the board (7 min)
We do: sketch a state diagram together as a class (8 min)
You do: in pairs, sketch a state diagram for a game idea (15 min)
Share out: one pair presents their diagram (5 min)
6th Period.connections: Your About Me pages are live and done — great work. Starting today we move into a brand-new unit, Game Design, where you'll build games instead of static pages. Tomorrow we build our first state machine in Sprite Lab.
